title: Old-Time Apple Storage
subtitle: Tips From a USDA Farmers' Bulletin
items: Keep as close to 32°F as you can
desc: Old-time apple storage tips from a USDA Farmers' Bulletin: keep apples cold and humid, wrap them in paper and sort often so they last into winter. Root cellar wisdom that still works.

title: Canning at High Altitude
subtitle: Adjust Above 1,000 Feet
desc: Canning at high altitude: above 1,000 feet, water bath times get longer and pressure canners need more pounds, per USDA home canning guidelines. Safe canning tips for beginners.

title: How to Dry Apples
subtitle: Easy Winter Snack
desc: How to dry apples at home in a dehydrator or oven: slice, pretreat, dry until leathery and condition before storing. Simple food preservation for a homemade winter pantry.

title: Fridge Food in a Power Outage
subtitle: What to Keep, What to Toss
items: When in doubt, throw it out
desc: Power outage food safety: how long food stays safe in the fridge and freezer and when to throw it out, based on USDA guidelines. Essential winter storm and emergency prep.

title: Leave Carrots in the Ground
subtitle: Harvest All Winter
desc: Overwinter carrots and parsnips in the garden under thick straw mulch and dig fresh roots all winter. An easy beginner vegetable garden tip for fall.
